decisive_items: a lifelong history of “white-attacks” of his fingers when cold (consistent with Raynaud’s phenomenon)
response.rationale: The patient's Raynaud's phenomenon is clearly described, while SLE is unlikely given elevated complement (C4 and CH50) and only a low-titer ANA without other SLE features.

rejected.why: Elevated complement and low-titer ANA are not supportive of SLE; no other SLE criteria are met.
